description: The board's photos are files `snapshots\accomp<record>.bmp` relative to the game's working directory. original\ (extracted from the cab), every instances\ copy and the cab hold no `snapshots` directory, so in every pinned recording the original's saveBmp fopen(`wb`) fails (returns 2, no file) and loadBmpSurface returns 6: no photo is drawn (the photo Image never gets a surface, Surface_blit3 returns 7). The installer's directory table in data1.hdr lists `Snapshots` between `SimsFX\Female` and `Sounds`; whether InstallShield creates it empty on a real install was not measured. The port writes and reads the file only when the files hold a `snapshots` directory (gfx_bulletin.cpp dir_exists = FindFirstFileA of `snapshots/*`), so it follows the install it runs over.
needed: a run of the stock installer (or a user's install) listing the install directory; a recording of the original with a `snapshots` folder present, its board frames as references

description: The photo is a file the original writes from the root surface, so the port writes it only with a graphics backend attached (its pixels exist only there); without one (segment and boot gates) no file is written where the original, with a `snapshots` directory, writes one. No pinned scenario has the directory (U-1840), so no gate sees a difference. The body writes through the context's GameFiles (the app's data directory, a test's overlay), the first gfx body to write a game file rather than a harness file.
needed: a decision whether the capture belongs to the simulation layer (a file with no pixels is not the original's either)

description: loadBmp sizes the pixel buffer with biSizeImage or, when 0, |biHeight| * biBitCount * biWidth (a bit count: 8x the bytes for a 24-bit file) and freads what the file holds; bytes past the file's end stay as malloc left them, which the port takes as 0. A size above 64 MB, or a width x height above 16 M pixels, is taken as the original's failed malloc / Surface_createFull (return 6). A file saveBmp wrote never reaches either case (its 0xc8 x 0xa0 body is read whole).
needed: only a hand-made file in `snapshots` reaches these

description: The board blits the photo's (0, 0, 0xc8, 0xa0) rectangle. The port copies min(0xc8, width) x min(0xa0, height) pixels clipped to the root; how jgld's slot +0x40 blit treats a source rectangle larger than the source surface (a bitmap smaller than 0xc8 x 0xa0, which saveBmp never writes) was not measured, and the Unicorn oracle covers the decode (loadBmpSurface) only, not that blit.
needed: the jgld blit16from16 rectangle clip under Unicorn with a small source

description: The bio EditBox is a window-tree child with its own surface; it is drawn only inside the bio loop (showScreen, redrawAll, leaveModal483d80, pumpMessages, Window::refreshFull, no clock call) and the editor's next pass blits the whole 800 x 600 background over it, so no reference frame can show it (cov_r_bio bio1_done / bio2_done are 0 px). The port reports `showCharacterEditor.bio` as unsupported drawing. A faithful body needs EditBox::drawContents (C2, no hook) on the EditBox's surface, the markup text drawn onto a non-root surface and the window tree's composition at Window::refreshFull; it also writes the scroll line [+0x57c], a GameState word the port's bio_entry never updates (a click in a bio longer than the box maps through it). HELD -> S3.19 (the S3 lead's decision, 2026-10-29; facts for it in 18_notes.md section 5).
needed: S3.19: the window-tree EditBox (emulator call oracle on drawContents)
